notes:
Summary: Cascade is a legacy media house (film archives, news reels, research reports) moving to a single searchable corpus for journalist and licensing teams. Focus is on retrieval-augmented workflows over very long documents (avg 6-12k words). Primary evaluation criteria are: query latency (p95/p99), cost per query at scale, freshness/ingest velocity, and reranker quality for precision-sensitive licensing workflows.

Scale & data: ~100M assets historically, expect 12-20M indexable blobs after dedupe and metadata split. Average raw doc length 6k-12k words; many multi-part series (multi-hour transcripts). Want incremental ingest: 5-10k new assets/week.

Current POC architecture: hybrid BM25 + dense retrieval. Precompute dense embeddings for chunks, store in customer-managed vector store (evaluating Redwood Dedicated store vs Milvus hosted in their VPC). Candidate set: retrieve top 200 dense + top 100 BM25, dedupe, then cross-encoder rerank top-K.

Chunking strategy under test: experiments running in parallel -
- fixed-token chunking 1k tokens non-overlapping (fast, smaller index, but context loss for entity spanning chunks)
- overlapping sliding windows 512 token stride 256 (better recall, index bloat ~2.1x)
- semantic chunking by paragraph/topic boundaries (using classifier) with size cap ~2k tokens (promising but slower to compute + harder to parallelize)
Goal: keep retrieval candidate size manageable while minimizing missed spans for long queries. Current sweet spot: 800-1200 token chunks with 10% overlap for transcripts.

Embedding + index decisions: evaluating text-embedding-3-small (costy) vs open models (sentence-transformers variants) for cost/latency tradeoff. Core ask: maintain recall while keeping per-query embedding cost near zero (precompute, incremental updates only). Considering hybrid ANN settings: HNSW ef/search tuning vs PQ for disk-backed nodes. Concern: index size ~20M vectors -> memory footprint, shard counts, and NUMA placement.

Reranker tuning: customer prefers a cross-encoder reranker for licensing queries (high precision). Plan: rerank only top 50 candidates (cost control) using a distilled cross-encoder (4-6 layers) tuned on internal labeling set (10k labeled q/doc pairs). Metrics target: NDCG@10 >= 0.82; reranker latency budget 30-80ms depending on scale. Fallback policy: if reranker slower than 150ms, degrade to lightweight pointwise scorer + serve with soft threshold.

Latency & cost targets: p95 end-to-end (retrieve+rerank+response) <= 400ms for single-doc queries, <= 800ms for multi-part retrieval flows. Cost sensitivity: want <$0.015 per complex query at 200 qps sustained (includes token generation for summarization). Optimization levers: batching reranks, cached rerank scores for popular queries, prefix/KV caching for generation, compaction/quantization for vectors.

Security & compliance: must pass SOC2 + KMS integration; on-prem option preferred for high-value licensing catalogs. Data residency: EU assets must remain in EU region; need model routing by region and audit logging for every retrieval.
